Overview

The acceptance record covers the complete measured request. The kernel view covers only the declared bounded profiler interval; no short-window kernel total is extrapolated over all 800 output tokens.

Measured Request

The prompt token count is bound to the outgoing manifest and the API usage record. Client wall time is retained as lifecycle evidence, but profiler stop and flush time make it unsuitable as normal serving latency.

Clock boundary The non-streaming client did not expose a measured time to first token. The bounded Nsight clock starts at the selected trace interval, not at client admission or server Receive.

How Each EAGLE Verification Step Works

Each target verification evaluates an ordered draft continuation. Acceptance is a contiguous prefix: after the first rejected draft position, later draft positions are not independently recoverable.

Draft

The EAGLE draft path proposes an ordered continuation of candidate tokens.

Target verification

The target model scores the draft continuation in one verification forward.

Accept a prefix

The matching prefix is accepted up to, but not beyond, the first rejection.

Emit

Accepted drafts plus one target, bonus, or fallback token form raw output for the step.

Continue

The next draft begins from the newly verified prefix until the exact output limit is reached.

EAGLE Execution Structure

The bounded trace contains two repeated CUDA graph families around named EAGLE control kernels. Draft-versus-target graph roles are trace inferences from repeated adjacency, not meanings assigned by the capture-local graph keys themselves.

Kernel Event Timeline

A deterministic browser-sized event view is placed on physical GPU lanes; full-event density and totals remain exact. Each GPU is split into Attention, FFN / GEMM, Control, and Communication sublanes. Thin amber lines are timestamped acceptance-report markers mapped into the profiler clock.

Capture-relative launches and intervals

Hover a visible interval for its raw kernel name, launch offset, duration, stream, and graph evidence. Rare EAGLE control events are drawn last so they remain discoverable.

Expanded Kernel Time Density

Each kernel interval is split across every bin it overlaps. Values are aggregate GPU-ms of kernel residency, not CUDA occupancy, utilization, useful FLOPs, or request latency.

Request and Capture Lifecycle

Client, profiler-control, and response-completion events are separate phases. Profiler export and stop behavior must not be folded into model-serving latency.

Evidence and Limitations

Source paths, hashes, selected-window counts, time bases, and inference boundaries stay visible so the report can be audited without opening Nsight first.

Interpretation limitPer-device kernel intervals are summed into aggregate residency. This is neither elapsed wall time nor a GPU-utilization percentage.
